name: MA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District carries an 11-point Democratic partisan lean
Dan Koh's dominant fundraising: $5.4M raised and $1.8M outside support vs $620K for Jones
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 96%
Open seat with no polls or expert ratings adds uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's eleven-point Democratic lean, Koh's roughly nine-to-one fundraising advantage with outside backing, and market pricing near 96 percent all point to a comfortable Democratic hold despite the open seat.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or a sharp shift in the national environment could narrow a margin that no public polling currently verifies.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Seth Moulton (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
The Sixth District carries an eleven-point Democratic lean, and the open-seat race to succeed Seth Moulton shows a wide resource gap. Dan Koh has raised about $5.4 million, holds roughly $1.1 million on hand, and draws about $1.8 million in outside support, while Republican Micah Jones has raised about $620,000 with no reported outside spending. Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 96 percent.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the money gap. The seat is rated Safe Democratic, though the open seat and absence of polling leave uncertainty somewhat wider than in a typical incumbent contest. A shift in the national environment or late outside spending would be the most visible signs of movement.
